history.heading: Ancient Jordan
paragraphs: Jordan has been inhabited since early prehistory. In biblical times it was home to the kingdoms of Ammon, Moab and Edom. The Nabataeans, Arab traders, built the spectacular rock-cut city of Petra, which flourished from around the 4th century BCE and is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
The region was later part of the Roman Empire, with cities such as Jerash (Gerasa), and the Byzantine Empire. The baptism site of Jesus at Bethany beyond the Jordan is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

history.heading: Islamic and Ottoman era
paragraphs: Arab Muslim armies conquered the region in the 7th century, and the Umayyads built desert castles such as Qusayr Amra. Crusaders, Ayyubids and Mamluks followed, and the Ottomans ruled from 1516 to 1918.

history.heading: The Hashemite kingdom
paragraphs: During the First World War, Sharif Hussein of Mecca led the Arab Revolt against the Ottomans. Britain then created the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921 under his son Abdullah. It became independent in 1946 as a kingdom.

In the 1948 war Jordan took control of the West Bank and East Jerusalem, which it lost to Israel in 1967. Large numbers of Palestinian refugees settled in Jordan. In 1970 the army fought Palestinian armed groups in "Black September". King Hussein, who reigned from 1952 to 1999, signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994. His son Abdullah II succeeded him.

culture.heading: Society
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language. Most Jordanians are Sunni Muslims, with a Christian minority. A large share of the population is of Palestinian origin, and the country has also hosted refugees from Iraq and Syria. Bedouin traditions of hospitality remain important.

Mansaf, lamb cooked in fermented yogurt sauce served over rice, is the national dish and is recognised by UNESCO. Wadi Rum's desert landscapes and the Dead Sea, the lowest point on land, are famous attractions.

politics.heading: Constitutional monarchy
paragraphs: Jordan is a constitutional monarchy in which the king holds broad powers, including appointing the government and the Senate. The House of Representatives is elected. Political reforms have been gradual, and dissent is restricted.

Jordan is a key ally of the United States and Western countries, maintains peace with Israel despite popular anger over the Palestinian conflict, and is custodian of Muslim and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem.

economy.heading: Limited resources
paragraphs: Jordan has few natural resources and is one of the most water-scarce countries in the world. The economy relies on services, tourism, phosphate and potash mining, pharmaceuticals, textiles, remittances and significant foreign aid.
Hosting large refugee populations, regional conflicts and high unemployment, especially among young people, are major challenges. The Jordanian dinar is pegged to the US dollar.
